evidence.finding: Billing queue skill mappings were updated at 09:15, exactly when the incident began.
Billing staffing fell from 12 to 9 agents after incident onset while General Service staffing increased from 19 to 22, indicating capacity redistribution rather than center-wide staff loss.
Billing service level fell 45.1 points to 44.7% and ASA rose 189%; General Service and Escalations improved, and Account Support remained above target.
All 49 scheduled agents remained logged in, and productive staffing was essentially unchanged across the incident boundary.
Aggregate offered volume increased only 2.6%, from 76 to 78 calls per interval, which does not support a center-wide demand spike.
Billing offered volume increased 26.9%, adding localized pressure after its staffed capacity was reduced.
Center service level declined from 88.4% before the incident to 76.5% afterward, while ASA increased from 29.8 to 43.1 seconds.

primary_root_cause_detail: A Billing skill-mapping change at 09:15 redirected three staffed agents from Billing to General Service. Billing capacity fell from 12 to 9 agents, after which Billing service level dropped from 89.8% to 44.7% and ASA increased 189%, while other queues remained stable or improved.
recommended_actions: Restore or correct the pre-incident Billing skill mappings and verify that Billing staffing returns to the intended level.
Audit the routing change for unintended transfer of Billing-skilled capacity to General Service.
Temporarily add Billing-skilled coverage while the queue recovers, accounting for the 26.9% localized volume increase.
Add post-change validation alerts for queue staffing redistribution, service-level divergence, and ASA increases.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Aggregate offered volume rose only 2.6%; localized Billing growth contributed but was not a center-wide surge and does not explain the synchronized agent redistribution.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant at 49, productive staffing was stable, and Billing's three-agent reduction was offset by a three-agent increase in General Service.
Aggregate AHT decreased 1.1%, and Billing AHT decreased 0.5% despite its severe service-level decline.
No platform event was recorded, and the impact was localized to Billing while other queues remained stable or improved.

stakeholder_summary: The incident was most likely caused by the 09:15 Billing routing change, which shifted three agents out of Billing and created a localized capacity imbalance. Billing performance collapsed while other queues improved; stable center staffing, near-stable aggregate demand, lower AHT, and no platform event rule out the main alternatives.
